topic: Getting an enterprise to actually adopt AI

slides.title: Start with a bleeding workflow
slides.body: Pick one process where delays already hit revenue or risk — not a safe side project. If AI fixes something painful, teams lean in instead of resisting.

slides.title: Design for minutes, not months
slides.body: Target workflows people do daily, in under 10 minutes. The more often it’s used, the faster behaviour shifts and the easier it is to prove adoption in hard numbers.

slides.title: Train by role, not by tool
slides.body: Don’t run generic ‘AI basics’. Sit with sales, ops, finance, legal and rebuild their actual tasks with them. Adoption follows when people see their own screen, not theory.

slides.title: Decide your risk lines early
slides.body: Publish clear red lines on data, approvals and audit trails before rollout. When people know what’s allowed, usage climbs instead of stalling in fear and ambiguity.

slides.title: Make usage a visible metric
slides.body: Track who’s using AI, on which tasks, and tie it to KPIs leaders already care about. When adoption is on dashboards, it stops being a side project and becomes work.

slides.title: Automate the boring, not the core
slides.body: Start by stripping admin from high-value roles — notes, summaries, routing, first drafts. Teams feel protected, not replaced, and they start asking for more, not less.

slides.title: Give one team end-to-end ownership
slides.body: Put a cross‑functional squad over AI use, training and guardrails. Without a clear owner, pilots scatter, standards diverge and the organisation never shifts as a whole.

slides.line: Need these 7 moves tailored to your org?
